card.intuition: A tool is a function the harness exposes for the agent to call - Read, Write, Bash, Search - and the only way an agent perceives and acts on its environment. The model never executes anything itself; it writes a structured call and the harness runs the function and returns the result.
card.analogy: A bank teller and a customer: the customer (model) fills out a withdrawal slip (tool call), but only the teller (harness) can open the vault - the slip itself moves no money.
card.time_complexity: Every tool call costs an extra model provider request, because the tool result must go back to the model before it can decide what to do next.
card.space_complexity: Tool definitions occupy context on every single request, so a large tool set has a standing token cost before any tool is ever called.
when_to_use: When the agent needs a capability, add a tool for it rather than routing everything through Bash
When you need to reach beyond the filesystem - a staging database or an external API
When a capable model is underperforming, remember that a narrow tool set makes a narrow agent
gotchas: Tool definitions load into context on every request, and many similar tools make the model worse at picking the right one
The model executes nothing itself - if the harness didn't run the call, nothing happened
Without a tool for something, the agent is completely blind to it; it can't reach past its tool list

steps.label: Define
steps.annotation: A tool is defined by a name, a description, and a parameter schema the harness sends to the model.

steps.label: Announce
steps.annotation: Tool definitions are sent with every model request, so the model knows what it may call.

steps.label: Choose
steps.annotation: The model picks a tool the same way it produces anything else, by writing tokens.

steps.label: Execute
steps.annotation: The model never executes; the harness reads the call, runs the function, and captures the result.

steps.label: Return
steps.annotation: The outcome goes back to the model in the next request before it decides what to do next.

exercise.prompt: Simulate the harness executing a tool call on behalf of the model. Unknown tools must raise, and arguments must be unpacked into the function.
hints: The harness rejects calls for tools the model doesn't know about
The model supplied arguments as a dict - spread them into the call
